chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Fear the governance, for the governance is but for the Imam who is knowledgeable in just judgement among the Muslims — for a Prophet or the successor of a Prophet.

key_terms.الْحُكُومَةُ: Governance/judgeship — refers to the authority to rule and adjudicate; in Shia jurisprudence, this denotes the political and judicial office that legitimately belongs only to the Imam
key_terms.الْعَالِمُ بِالْقَضَاءِ: The one knowledgeable in adjudication — specifies the required qualification for the holder of governance: comprehensive jurisprudential knowledge for dispensing just verdicts
key_terms.وَصِيُّ نَبِيٍّ: Successor/vicegerent of a Prophet — designates the divinely appointed successor (wasi) to a Prophet, i.e., the Imam in Shia theology

ai.seo_question: Who has the right to govern and judge according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a stern warning against assuming positions of governance and judicial authority without proper qualification. He declares that legitimate governance belongs exclusively to the Imam who possesses comprehensive knowledge of just adjudication among Muslims — and that this authority is reserved only for a Prophet or his designated successor (wasi). This teaching was directed to Shia jurists and followers who might be tempted to accept official positions under Abbasid rule, warning them that such positions usurp a right belonging solely to the infallible Imam.
